## Knowledge pipeline (`kb`)

This repository is a knowledge base maintained through a `kb` CLI. **`kb` never calls a model.**
Commands that need judgment run in two phases: without a draft they emit a self-contained JSON
task, and with one they validate your answer and act on it deterministically. You supply the
judgment; the CLI supplies the structure and every decision that can be made by rule.

| command | use it when |
|---|---|
| `kb assess <file> [--verdict v.json]` | Judge whether a staged source is worth promoting into a concept, using the repo's promotion rubric. Use after kb-ingest, or when asked whether something is worth keeping, promoting or discarding. |
| `kb audit [--only <check>] [--findings f.json]` | Semantic lint — contradictions, stale claims, concept gaps, graph rot. Use after a batch of promotions, when the corpus feels inconsistent, or on a maintenance pass. |
| `kb cards <slug> [--draft c.json] [--apply]` | Create or refresh the spaced-repetition flashcard deck for a concept. Use when asked to make, update or improve flashcards or study material for a concept. |
| `kb context --for <task> <args>` | Compile the exact context a task needs — target notes, binding policy, graph neighbours, prior artifacts — as one deterministic bundle. Use before drafting cards, reviewing a promotion, judging an audit pair, or answering from the corpus. |
| `kb facets [--sample N] [--draft f.json] [--apply]` | Classify concepts against the repo's closed facet axes — domain, maturity and source type. Use when notes are unclassified, or when asked to categorise, tag or organise concepts. |
| `kb ingest <url...>` | Fetch a URL into the knowledge base's staging area as a reviewable source note. Use when the user shares a link, article or repo they want captured, or says to ingest, capture or save a source. |
| `kb link check | suggest | --draft l.json [--apply]` | Find isolated or one-way-linked concepts and propose reciprocal cross-links. Use when a concept is unreachable, after promoting a new concept, or when asked to improve connections between notes. |
| `kb promote <slug> [--draft d.json] [--apply]` | Turn an assessed staging note into one or more concept notes. Use after kb-assess routes to promote or split, or when asked to write up a staged source as a concept. |
| `kb query "<question>" [--domain D] [--maturity M] [--answer a.json]` | Ask the knowledge base a question and get back the relevant concepts with their cross-references. Use whenever the answer might already be in the corpus — before researching, before ingesting a new source, or when asked what the vault says about something. |
| `kb support <slug> [--verdicts v.json]` | Judge whether a concept's citations actually support its claims. Use when validating a note's evidence, after revalidate reports drift, or when asked whether a source really backs what the note says. |
| `kb verify | kb index` | Validate the knowledge base and regenerate its index. Use before committing, after any bulk change, or when asked whether the vault is healthy or consistent. |

**Rules that are not negotiable** (`.kb/POLICY.md`):

- Never delete or rewrite a wikilink. An unresolved link is a recorded gap, not an error.
- Never modify text inside inline code spans or fenced code blocks.
- Never delete a file. A `discard` verdict is a recommendation.
- Bulk writers dry-run by default; `--apply` needs a clean tree so the change stays reviewable.

Run `kb verify` before committing. It is the contract — CI runs it, and these instructions cannot enforce anything.
